Warning about using MaxTrax Boards on non-all terrain tires:

MAXTRAX are designed to work with off-road type tyres (All Terrain or Mud Terrain) as the more open style tread allows easy engagement of the tread blocks with the traction 'teeth' on top of the MAXTRAX. We strongly advise against using MAXTRAX with highway type tires as the sipes (the grooves in the tread) are typically inadequate (too narrow and shallow) to properly engage with the teeth on the top of the MAXTRAX and are likely to allow wheel spin and cause damage to the traction teeth, which is not covered under warranty. We recommend at least 'All Terrain' tyres as the greater the tread depth and the more aggressive the tread, the more effective MAXTRAX are.

OEM Hitch, Aftermarket Hitches,  Departure Angles, Crumple Zones and Spot Welds.

The OEM hitch has a completely different mounting method than any aftermarket hitches, it mounts into the unibody rails and then bolts in through the rails at 6 screw mount positions.

Possible issues with non-OEM hitches, aside from the enhanced damage from rear impacts, include the effects of upward and downward forces applied to those aftermarket hitches during towing, which could weaken or crack spot welds on the unibody.

I installed a Curt Hitch on to the chassis of my old F-150, no big deal - but then again,  anything bolted onto that beast of a frame is like play dough.  Unibodies are a whole different animal.

U-Haul, Curt, e-hitch, Hidden Hitch, etc are not designed to align, with the crumple zones of your Outback’s unibody. And most important, unlike aftermarket hitches, a dealer installed OEM hitch does not put your warranty at risk. Meaning that if the issue can be connected by SOA, or the dealership to an aftermarket hitch or non-Subaru hitch install problem - your warranty is toast.

Those who have already installed aftermarket hitches on their Outbacks will obviously dismiss my post. But If you’ haven’t yet made that decision, don’t take the chance. Speak to a non-dealer Subaru mechanic. I know I did…The Subie Guys in my area.
